title: Once Props
description: Remember expensive values on the client and skip them on later visits.
body: Once props are expensive values that rarely change. The client remembers them across visits and tells the server which keys it holds with X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props . Behavior - The value is left out on later visits, but the onceProps entry stays so the client keeps its copy. - .Fresh() sends the value even when the client has it. - Partial reloads always resolve once props that the reload asks for. - Expiry is computed from the registered TimeProvider , so tests can use FakeTimeProvider . - .As(key) and .Until(ttl) imply once. - Sharing a key between pages lets the client reuse one value across them. Keys The default key is the prop path. Use .As("billing-plans") when the same value is exposed under different names, or when you want a stable key across page changes. Two props that share a key are treated as the same client value. Only share a key when the values are actually the same. When in doubt, use the default prop path. Expiry .Until(TimeSpan) sets expiresAt in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The client stops treating the key as loaded after that time and requests the value again. The server leaves the value out only when the client lists the key in X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props . Shared once props This is the equivalent of Laravel's shareOnce : the client keeps the value across visits. Testing InertiaPage.OnceProps exposes the metadata: Revisit the page with the same client and assert that the prop is missing while onceProps remains.

title: Build ForgetMeNot
description: A complete Inertia.Net todo app with login, public lists, paginated loading, reminders and SSR.
headings: 10. Add the root template and client entry
body: ForgetMeNot is a small but realistic todo application. People sign in, keep private lists, share selected lists publicly, and get reminders when something is due. The interesting parts are the boundaries: authentication, public pages without an account, paginated lists that load as you scroll, and a background worker that must not block a request. This guide builds it with Minimal APIs, EF Core, React and Inertia.Net. The code is trimmed for readability; put each section in its own file when you build the real thing. The authentication, public-page, cache and Bun SSR patterns here follow Inkwell, CarParker and TechLandierDistributed. Use them when you want a complete, runnable version of each pattern. What ForgetMeNot does - Email and password registration and login with a cookie - Private todo lists, with completed items kept out of the way - Public read-only lists at an unguessable URL - Todo items loaded in pages and merged by Inertia's InfiniteScroll - Due dates and one-time reminder delivery - Deferred dashboard stats and reminders so the page renders immediately - SSR and Bun in the production container Deferred, cached and scroll props used below. How Scroll and InfiniteScroll fit together. Forms, error bags and redirects. The production renderer. 1. Create the app The frontend uses React and the Inertia v3 client. Bun is assumed here; npm works the same way. The project layout: 2. Model the domain Keep the public shape separate from the database entity. A todo list owns a stable, random public slug, and a reminder is just a time on the item plus the time it was last sent. RemindAt is when the reminder becomes due. RemindedAt makes delivery idempotent: a retry, a restart, or two workers will not send the same reminder forever. For a production app, use EF migrations. For this guide, db.Database.EnsureCreated() is enough to get moving. The page props use small records instead of exposing entities: 3. Wire authentication and Inertia The cookie is the session. Inertia never sees a token, and antiforgery still protects the forms. UseAuthentication() must run before UseInertiaAntiforgery() if the token is bound to the signed-in user. Behind Coolify or another TLS-terminating proxy, configure forwarded headers so the Secure cookie and absolute URLs use https . auth is a shared prop, so every page receives the signed-in user without repeating a query in every endpoint. The client can render the header from usePage().props.auth . 4. Register and sign in The forms post to Minimal API endpoints. WithInertiaValidation() turns attribute failures into a redirect back with errors , which is what useForm() expects. The login page only needs useForm : 5. List the private dashboard The index is intentionally cheap: it counts items, then loads the reminder panel and the stats after the page is visible. On the client, keeps the page interactive while the sidebar loads: 6. Load todo items in pages A list can contain thousands of items. Send one page, merge the next page into the client value, and let ask for more as the user reaches the bottom. Scroll merges the data array inside items and adds the paging metadata. The React page does not need to know the page number: This is the virtual loading model: the browser only DOM-renders the pages it has requested, and Inertia requests the next page when the sentinel approaches the viewport. If a page has thousands of loaded items, add windowing on top, but keep the scroll trigger outside the virtualized window. Most todo lists do not need that extra layer. Before the list page, create lists from the dashboard: 7. Add and complete items Writes use the same validation and flash conventions as the login form. The tag invalidation is why the dashboard stats were cached with user:{userId} . A completed item changes the counts, so the cached stats must disappear. 8. Share a list publicly Add a public route that does not require a login. Use a random slug instead of the numeric id, and never expose RemindAt or anything else private. Generate the slug once when the list is created: The public page is a quiet read-only view: A public list should not reveal the owner's email, private lists or reminder settings. Keep the public DTO explicit; do not return the entity. 9. Send reminders once A hosted service polls for due items and marks them after delivery. This is deliberately simple: one instance, one sweep per minute. For several app replicas, use a durable queue with leases (TickerQ, Hangfire, a database outbox) and claim each due item atomically. RemindedAt still prevents duplicates, but the sweep itself must not run on every replica without coordination. When a todo is saved with RemindAt in the future, the next sweep picks it up. The dashboard's deferred list shows the reminders that have not fired yet. 10. Add the root template and client entry The root template is the same one used by every Inertia.Net app: @inertiajs/vite can generate the resolver for you; then createInertiaApp() is enough. See Client setup. 11. Test the interesting paths Use Inertia.Net.Testing for page assertions and deferred props. The public route is the one most likely to leak private data, so test its exact props. For the public list, sign out first and assert that the owner's email and reminder fields are absent. The test is as valuable as the endpoint. 12. Run it in production Build both the client and the SSR bundle with Bun: The app reads ssr/ssr.js and starts it with Bun. The production container from the docs site shows the same pattern: ASP.NET Core runtime, the Bun binary, the published app, wwwroot/build and ssr/ baked into the image. For deployment details, see Server-side rendering and Deploying behind a proxy. ForgetMeNot itself only needs a persistent SQLite file and a shared Data Protection key ring if you ever run more than one instance; the public route does not need a session. What the samples add The published samples are deliberately more complete than this guide: - Inkwell keeps shared auth and notifications behind Once and Cache , wraps only public post pages in a custom IInertiaRootView , and runs Bun SSR inside the app image. - CarParker uses Mongo transactions for bookings, tags its cached props for invalidation, and serves public pages with the same Scroll / InfiniteScroll shape as ForgetMeNot. - TechLandierDistributed separates the web, worker, realtime and SSR roles, points Inertia:SsrUrls at a Bun SSR pool, and exposes /health and /alive for the proxy. - All three build the client and SSR bundle with Bun, ship only the Bun binary in the runtime image, and use the same /health container check. Browse the sample source for the complete implementations.

title: Quick Start
description: Add Inertia.Net to an ASP.NET Core app, create the root template and render your first page.
body: Already using the starter template? Its services, middleware, root template and frontend are configured for you. These steps are for adding Inertia to an existing app or building one manually. Every app needs the same four things: 1. Register the services Choose one backend style. All three use the same protocol middleware and the same Render(...) result. AddValidation() enables the Minimal API integration used by .WithInertiaValidation() . UseInertiaAntiforgery() issues the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and validates every unsafe request, so forms work from the first commit. 2. Add the root template The root template is an HTML file in the content root. The default name is app.html . Remove @viteReactRefresh for Vue and Svelte. @inertia is required. The other tokens are described in Pages and responses. Make sure app.html is copied to the output and publish directory: 3. Create the page component The page name passed to Render must match the client resolver. With @inertiajs/vite the resolver maps ClientApp/pages/ automatically. The client entry only needs to start Inertia: Pass your own resolve and setup functions to createInertiaApp . The client setup page shows both forms for React, Vue and Svelte. 4. Run it Start Vite and ASP.NET Core in two terminals, from the project directory: Open the URL printed by dotnet watch (not the Vite URL). The first visit to / should display “Hello from .NET”. For production, build the client and publish the app: Deploy wwwroot/build and app.html with the published app. Where to go next Vite configuration and the React, Vue and Svelte entries. Lazy, deferred, merged and cached page data. Redirects, error bags and Precognition. Render the first visit on Node.

title: Client Setup
description: Configure Vite and the React, Vue or Svelte client for an Inertia.Net app.
body: Inertia.Net speaks the Inertia.js v3 protocol. Install a v3 client package; v2 clients are not supported. Install the client Run the npm commands from the ASP.NET Core project directory (the one containing your .csproj ). The starter templates use ClientApp/pages . The manual examples below use resources/js/Pages . Keep the resolver, file paths and Vite entry consistent with the layout you choose. Vite configuration The same Vite config works for every client; only the framework plugin changes. Add these fields to package.json : The manifest key of the entry ( resources/js/app.tsx ) is what you pass to @vite("...") . Client entry The optional @inertiajs/vite plugin resolves pages and mounts the app for you. With it, the entry is just: Without the plugin, provide the resolver and setup yourself. Pages A page file receives the props from Render(...) as normal component props. Inertia.Net can write TypeScript declarations for your page props, shared props and flash data. See TypeScript types. Development workflow Open the ASP.NET Core URL, not the Vite URL. In Development the app reads wwwroot/hot and renders the Vite tags; in production it reads the manifest. For production: Node is needed to build the assets and only needed at runtime when SSR is enabled. Using @inertiajs/vite The plugin also contributes the SSR dev endpoint and page resolution. Add it before the hot-file plugin: Keep the SSR listener on loopback: the renderer trusts its output and has no authentication. The SSR guide covers the full setup.

title: DevTools & Development Checks
description: Record visits for the Inertia DevTools extension and catch missing page components during development.
body: The Inertia DevTools browser extension shows every visit, its props, headers and page state. Inertia.Net implements the server protocol. Enable DevTools Each request through UseInertia() gets an X-Inertia-Devtools-Id and an entry in memory (per browser tab, at most MaxEntriesPerTab and MaxEntries , for MaxAge ): request type, timings, headers, bodies, the page object and its props metadata. The first page carries the discovery tag the extension reads. Values of names containing password , secret , token , authorization , cookie or api key are replaced with [REDACTED] in props, bodies and headers. Add names with RedactedKeys . Nothing leaves the app. Sensitive query parameters are also redacted in recorded request/page URLs, redirects and URL headers; actual application URLs are unchanged. Malformed JSON bodies are omitted. Only eligible Inertia text bodies with a known length up to MaxBodyBytes are buffered; unknown-length nonseekable bodies are omitted as streamed, so recording does not spool bulk requests to disk. Outside Development nothing is recorded unless Enabled = true , and the read API answers only requests that Authorize accepts ( 404 otherwise). With Pages.Directory set, entries link the component to its file. Page component check In Development, Render throws when the component has no page file, naming the closest one: Names match exactly, as the client resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems. Outside Development there is no check and no file access. Pages.Extensions lists the file types: .tsx , .jsx , .ts , .js , .vue and .svelte by default. Generated TypeScript The development startup also writes TypeScript declarations when o.TypeScript.OutputPath is set. It only writes the file when the content changed. See TypeScript types. What to check before deploying - Pages.Directory can stay configured; it is inactive outside Development. - DevTools recording is off unless explicitly enabled. - The generated TypeScript file is committed if the client build type-checks in CI. - Production logs do not contain the DevTools read API. Install the Inertia DevTools extension, open your app in Development, and use the extension's panel. The server entries are correlated by the X-Inertia-Devtools-Id header.

title: Vite Integration
description: Manifest tags, the dev-server hot file, asset base URLs, prefetching and CSP nonces.
body: ViteAssets (a singleton, also usable directly as vite.RenderTags(httpContext, "resources/js/app.tsx") ) renders the tags for the @vite(...) token and the tag helper. Production In production Inertia.Net reads wwwroot/build/.vite/manifest.json (falling back to wwwroot/build/manifest.json for older Vite). It parses the manifest once and pre-renders the tags to UTF-8. For each entry it emits, in order: 1. for the entry's CSS and the CSS of its static imports, recursively and deduplicated; 2. for the entry file; 3. for each static import. URLs are {PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}/{file} so apps under a path base work, or {AssetBaseUrl}/{file} . An entry missing from the manifest throws with the list of available entries. A missing manifest throws with the paths it looked in. Development While the dev server runs, the tags are @vite/client and the entry from the dev server origin, plus the React Refresh preamble for @viteReactRefresh . The dev server counts as running when: - o.Vite.DevServerUrl is set (always, in any environment), or - the environment is Development and the hot file ( wwwroot/hot by default) exists and contains the origin. The hot file is written by your Vite config. The @inertiajs/vite plugin does not write one, so the samples include a small plugin that does. Built assets are served from /build/ , so the Vite base is /build/ for a build. The dev server must serve from the root because Inertia.Net emits {origin}/@vite/client and {origin}/{entry} . Use base: command === 'build' ? '/build/' : '/' . Options Only plain http(s) origins without quotes or markup are accepted from the hot file or DevServerUrl , because the origin is echoed into a script. With AssetBaseUrl set, Vite's own base must match so lazily imported chunks resolve against the CDN too: Prefetching Page components resolved with lazy import.meta.glob are separate chunks that the browser downloads only when a page needs them. o.Vite.Prefetch downloads them after the page loads, at low priority, so the next navigation does not wait: The tags get one small inline script with the list of chunks the entries can import later (dynamic imports, then their static imports and CSS), minus those already loaded. It is rendered once per entry set. Content Security Policy With a nonce-based CSP, set o.CspNonce to the request's nonce. Every script and stylesheet tag Inertia.Net writes then carries it: the page , the Vite tags, the React refresh preamble and the prefetch script (whose links get it too). The nonce must be base64 or base64url; anything else throws. Cached tags are split where the nonce goes, so a nonce costs one copy of the tag bytes per request and no re-rendering. Use app.UseStaticFiles() with a long Cache-Control for /build/assets , or app.MapStaticAssets() when the client is built before dotnet publish . See Deploying.

title: Props
description: Lazy, optional, deferred, merged, once, cached and rescued page data.
body: Props are the data a page receives. Render(component, props) takes an InertiaProps , a string-keyed dictionary, or a typed object. Nested InertiaProps and dictionaries are walked, so props can be nested at any depth. Every page has an errors prop. Its key order is errors , shared props, then page props. The prop factories C\ Behavior --- --- ["title"] = "Hi" A plain value. Sent on every response that includes the key. Prop(() = ...) Lazy: the loader runs only when the prop is part of the response. Always(value) or Always(() = ...) Sent even when a partial reload does not ask for it. Optional(() = ...) Never sent on the first visit, only when a partial reload asks for it. Defer(() = ..., group: "name") Left out of the first response. The client loads it right away with its group. Merge(value) The client appends the new value to its current one. DeepMerge(value) The client deep merges the value. Once(() = ...) Resolved once and remembered by the client. Scroll(page, wrapper: "data", metadata) An infinite-scroll prop with paging metadata. Every lazy factory ( Prop , Always , Optional , Defer , Merge , DeepMerge , Once , Scroll ) accepts five loader shapes: The token is HttpContext.RequestAborted . An async lambda always binds to the awaiting overload, never to “a prop whose value is a Task”. Fluent methods mutate and return the same instance: .Once(key?, until?) , .As(key) , .Until(ttl) , .Fresh() , .Append(path?, matchOn?) , .Prepend(path?, matchOn?) , .DeepMerge() , .MatchOn(params keys) , .Defer(group) , .WithGroup(group) , .Rescue() , .Parallel() , .Cache(key, duration) and .Cache(key, duration, staleFor?, tags?) . Resolution order Loaders run sequentially by default, in prop order, and only when their prop is included in the response. That makes a scoped EF Core DbContext safe to use in several loaders. The page is buffered before it is sent, so a loader that throws never produces a half-written 200 . Parallel props Mark independent async loaders with .Parallel() to start them together: - Only Task and ValueTask loaders can be parallel. Parallel() throws for values and synchronous loaders. - At most InertiaOptions.Props.MaxConcurrency loaders run at once per render (default 4). - Top-level props and props inside literal objects ( InertiaProps and other string-keyed dictionaries) start early. Elsewhere they resolve in turn. - Loaders of props that are not part of the response never start. - If a loader fails, the others are cancelled and awaited, and the render fails with the first failure in prop order. A Rescue() d prop fails alone. A parallel loader must not use the request's DbContext or other non-thread-safe scoped services, and must not touch HttpContext . Give each loader its own context through IDbContextFactory or its own scope. Deferred props Defer leaves the prop out of the first response and lists it under deferredProps . The client asks for each group as soon as the page is mounted. See Deferred props for the client component and the request rules. Merge props The full behavior is in Merging props. Once props When the client already holds the key it sends X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props ; the value is left out while the onceProps entry stays. See Once props. Cached props .Cache(key, duration) keeps a prop's value as JSON in the cache (the app's IMemoryCache by default). A hit costs neither the query nor serialization. Every request that uses a key gets the same value. Put the user, tenant or anything else the value depends on in the key. Keys live in their own cache space and cannot collide with the app's own entries. Only loading changes: optional, deferred, merged, once and scroll props keep their behavior, and their metadata is written from the cache too. A parallel cached prop does not start its loader on a hit. A rescued failure is not cached. Removing and replacing values. Inject IInertiaCache where the data changes: ClearPropsAsync() removes every cached prop and ClearSsrAsync() every cached render. SetPropAsync serializes the value as a prop of its type would, and takes the same staleFor and tags . Stale-while-revalidate. staleFor keeps serving a value after its duration. The first request that reads a stale value gets it at once, and the loader runs after the response has been sent. Past duration + staleFor the loader runs during the request again. - The refresh runs in the response's completion callbacks, before the request's services are disposed, so it can keep using the request's scoped services. It must not touch HttpContext . - One refresh runs per key and app instance at a time. A refresh that finds the value fresh again skips its loader. - A refresh that fails is logged as a warning and keeps the stale value; the next stale read tries again. Another store. Props and SSR renders live in an IInertiaCacheStore . Register your own singleton before or after AddInertia() : The store gets and sets byte arrays by InertiaCacheKey , removes by key and by tag, and reads unknown formats as a miss. While a page renders, a store that throws is logged (at most once every 30 seconds) and counts as a miss; IInertiaCache lets the exception through. Typed page props A typed object is AOT-friendly: it is walked through its JsonTypeInfo , and members of type InertiaProp are resolved by Inertia.Net while the rest is serialized normally. Register UsersPage and its value types in your JsonSerializerContext under Native AOT. Anonymous types work only when reflection-based serialization is enabled, so not under AOT. Dot keys A top-level key containing dots is unpacked. ["user.name"] = "Ann" becomes "user": { "name": "Ann" } . BigInteger safety With o.PreserveBigIntegers = true , integers beyond ±(2^53 − 1) are written as {"$bigint":"9007199254740993"} and the page gets "preserveBigIntegers": true . Rescue .Rescue() keeps a page alive when one prop fails: If the loader throws, the exception is logged, the prop is left out of props , and its path goes to "rescuedProps": ["recommendations"] . Without .Rescue() the exception propagates normally. Cancellation of the request is never rescued.

title: Merging Props
description: Append, prepend, deep merge and match items instead of replacing the client's value.
body: By default a reloaded prop replaces the client's value. Merge props tell the client to combine them. This is how pagination, chat messages and incremental lists work. C\ Metadata Client behavior --- --- --- Merge(v) mergeProps: ["key"] Append to the existing array Prop(...).Prepend() prependProps: ["key"] Prepend Merge(v).Append("path") mergeProps: ["key.path"] Append at a nested path Prop(...).Prepend("path") prependProps: ["key.path"] Prepend at a nested path DeepMerge(v) deepMergeProps: ["key"] Deep merge objects and arrays .MatchOn("id") matchPropsOn: ["key.id"] Replace items with the same id instead of duplicating them .Append("path", matchOn: "id") matchPropsOn: ["key.path.id"] The match key is relative to the nested path Nested paths The path before the wrapper stays on the client; only the value below the path is merged. Resetting a merge The client can ask for a fresh value instead of a merge by listing the path in X-Inertia-Reset : Metadata is skipped for paths in the reset list, and on partial reloads for paths the reload did not ask for. Match on a stable key .MatchOn("id") replaces an item with the same key instead of appending a duplicate. Use a stable, unique key from your data. Without it, incremental updates append every item again. Deep merge DeepMerge recursively combines objects. Arrays are merged by index; use MatchOn when you need item identity. On a partial reload, merge metadata is only emitted for paths the reload asked for. Always still applies independently.

title: Redirects and History
description: Redirects, Back, Location, history encryption, clearing and URL fragments.
body: Inertia requests follow redirects with XHR, which is not always what the browser would do. Inertia.Net adjusts redirect responses so the client behaves correctly. Redirect helpers Back() only follows a Referer that is an http(s) URL with the request's own host and port. This prevents an open redirect. The scheme is not compared, so it works behind a TLS-terminating proxy; on HTTPS an http Referer is upgraded to https . What the middleware changes Situation Result --- --- 302 for PUT, PATCH or DELETE Changed to 303 See Other , so the browser follows with a GET Redirect to another origin, non-prefetch 409 with X-Inertia-Location : the client makes a full visit instead of an XHR the browser would block Redirect whose Location contains , non-prefetch 409 with X-Inertia-Redirect : the client performs a full visit that keeps the fragment Location(url) 409 + X-Inertia-Location for Inertia requests, a plain 302 otherwise Empty 200 response Redirect back (302, or 303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE), falling back to the app root Vary Vary: X-Inertia is added to every response through the middleware Turn off external redirect conversion with o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false if the app intentionally redirects to another origin. Pages without a handler Maps GET and HEAD to Render("About", props) , like Laravel's Route::inertia . In MVC, return this.InertiaView(props); renders the action's own component, {Controller}/{Action} by default. AddInertiaMvc(o = o.ComponentResolver = ctx = ...) changes the rule. History encryption encryptHistory is written as true only when set and is not carried across redirects. The Inertia client encrypts its history state with the page's key. Clearing history clearHistory goes through the state store, applies to the next page rendered after the redirect(s), then is consumed. It is typically used before a redirect after logout. Preserving a fragment By default a redirect loses the URL fragment. PreserveFragment() keeps it across the next redirect. The client receives preserveFragment: true on the next page. Page URL The page object's url is PathBase, Path and QueryString. Behind a proxy that rewrites paths, set o.UrlResolver to return the URL the browser sees: Flash data, errors, clearHistory and preserveFragment share the state store. By default that is an encrypted cookie; see Flash data.

title: Deferred Props
description: Load slow page sections after the first render, in groups.
body: Defer leaves a prop out of the first response and lists it under deferredProps . The client requests each group with a partial reload as soon as the page is mounted. The page becomes interactive without waiting for the slow data. Props in the same group load in one request. Different groups load in parallel requests. deferredProps is only produced on non-partial renders. The client Vue uses from @inertiajs/vue3 ; Svelte uses the matching component from @inertiajs/svelte . Combining with other props A deferred prop can also be merged, once or rescued: The metadata combines: deferredProps lists the group, mergeProps lists the path, and onceProps records the key. Deferred scroll props A deferred Scroll(...) prop reports "posts.data" just like a resolved one. This is a deliberate fix of an inertia-laravel quirk: Testing See Testing for the full assertion API. Deferred props are for data the page can render without. If the page cannot be meaningful until the data arrives, a normal prop is simpler.

title: Configuration
description: InertiaOptions, Vite, SSR, props, state and the middleware and result API.
body: All configuration is passed to AddInertia . Options marked “Development only” do nothing in other environments. AddInertia(o = ...) : InertiaOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- RootView "app.html" Root template relative to the content root (a Razor view name with UseRazorRootView ). Paths outside the content root are refused. RootElementId "app" Id of the root element and the data-page script. Version null Asset version. null means the Vite manifest hash, or "" without one. VersionResolver null Func per-request version; wins over Version when non-null. EncryptHistory false Encrypt browser history state of every page. WithAllErrors false Send every validation message per field instead of the first. PreserveBigIntegers false Emit integers beyond ±(2^53−1) as {"$bigint":"..."} . ExposeSharedPropKeys true List top-level shared keys in sharedProps . CspNonce null Func : the request's CSP nonce. ConvertExternalRedirects true Turn an Inertia redirect to another origin into 409 + X-Inertia-Location . UrlResolver null Func : the page url . Pages.Directory / Pages.Extensions null / .tsx .jsx .ts .js .vue .svelte Development check that a rendered component has a page file. TypeScript.OutputPath , .Page (component) , .SharedProps () , .FlashData () null TypeScript declarations, written in Development. Share(key, value) / Share(key, Func ) none Shared props. o.Vite : ViteOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- PublicDirectory "wwwroot" Web root containing the build directory and hot file. BuildDirectory "build" Vite output directory under PublicDirectory ; also the URL prefix. ManifestPath null Manifest path relative to the content root. null = {PublicDirectory}/{BuildDirectory}/.vite/manifest.json , then manifest.json . HotFilePath null Hot file relative to the content root. null = {PublicDirectory}/hot . Read in Development only. DevServerUrl null Dev server origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173 . When set, dev tags always render. AssetBaseUrl null Replaces {PathBase}/{BuildDirectory} as the URL prefix of built assets. Prefetch None Waterfall or Aggressive : prefetch code-split chunks after load. PrefetchConcurrency 3 Chunks Waterfall downloads at a time. o.Ssr : SsrOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- Mode Disabled Disabled , Preferred or Required . Disabled cannot be overridden per response. Urls empty ( http://127.0.0.1:13714 ) SSR server base URLs. Not used with UseNodeProcess() . Timeout 5 s Total deadline per render. Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan disables it. MaxResponseBytes 16 MiB Limit on actual response bytes, including errors and chunked responses. MaxPageBytes 2 MiB Pages whose JSON is larger render on the client without a call. BundlePath null Skip SSR while this file is missing, unless the Vite dev server runs. ExcludePaths empty Request paths never rendered on the server (exact, or a trailing for a prefix). Concurrency.MaxActive 8 Renders in flight per server from this app instance; 0 for no limit. Concurrency.MaxQueued 32 Renders waiting for a slot per server. Concurrency.QueueTimeout 250 ms How long a render waits for a slot. CircuitBreaker.Enabled true Pause servers that keep failing. CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold 5 Consecutive failures that open a server's circuit. CircuitBreaker.BreakDuration 10 s How long an open circuit skips the server before one probe. Cache.Duration Zero (off) Reuse a render for this long when the page JSON is the same. Cache.StaleFor Zero Serve stale while re-rendering. Cache.MaxBytes 64 MiB Size of the default store's render cache. UseNodeProcess(configure?) off Start and supervise Node SSR processes (sets Mode = Preferred when Disabled ). Per response: Render(...).WithSsr(SsrMode) and .WithoutSsr() . The full SSR options are in Server-side rendering. o.Props : InertiaPropsOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- MaxConcurrency 4 Loaders marked .Parallel() that run at once per render. Must be positive. o.State : InertiaStateOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- CookieName ".Inertia.State" Cookie name (cookie store) or session key (session store). CookieSecurePolicy SameAsRequest When the state cookie is Secure . UseSession() off Use ISession instead of the encrypted cookie. AddInertiaMvc(o = o.UseTempDataStateStore()) off Use MVC TempData. Inertia.Net.Mvc package. Middleware and endpoint API API Description --- --- services.AddInertia(configure?) Registers services and options. app.UseInertia() The protocol middleware. Before the endpoints; after UseSession() when used. app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(configure?) Issues the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and validates unsafe requests ( 419 on failure). app.MapInertia(pattern, component, props?) GET and HEAD endpoint that renders the component. services.AddInertiaDevTools(configure?) / app.MapInertiaDevTools() DevTools recorder and read API. app.UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN") Only writes the token cookie; validation is up to you. endpoint.WithInertiaValidation() Minimal API: validation failures redirect back with errors. endpoint.WithInertiaPrecognition() Minimal API: WithInertiaValidation() plus Precognition. healthChecks.AddInertiaSsr(...) SSR health check from the gateway's state. mvc.AddInertiaMvc(o = o.UseRazorRootView("App")) MVC filter, optional Razor root view and component resolver. config.UseInertia(configure?) FastEndpoints: validation redirect and Precognition. Render(component, props?) InertiaResult : .WithStatusCode , .WithRootView , .WithViewData , .WithSsr , .WithoutSsr , .WithSsrCache . Location(url) InertiaLocationResult . Back(fallback = "~/") InertiaBackResult : .WithErrors , .WithFlash . httpContext.Inertia() InertiaFeature : Share , Flash , WithErrors , ClearHistory , EncryptHistory , PreserveFragment . Send.InertiaAsync(...) , Send.InertiaLocationAsync(...) , Send.InertiaBackAsync(...) FastEndpoints Send extensions.
