title: Pages and Responses
description: Render components, use MapInertia, and understand the root template and response status codes.
body: An Inertia page is a component name plus a set of props. The server writes the page object into the response; the client resolves the component and renders it. Rendering a page Render(component, props) returns an InertiaResult . The component name must match your client-side page resolver exactly, including case. Render accepts an InertiaProps (an ordered string-keyed dictionary), any IDictionary , or a typed object whose properties are the props. Nested InertiaProps and dictionaries are walked at any depth. Every page has an errors prop (an empty object when there are no errors). Key order is errors , shared props, then page props. Per-response options InertiaResult builds on the response without changing the component: Method Effect --- --- .WithStatusCode(int) Sets the HTTP status of the page response .WithRootView(string) Uses another root template for this response .WithViewData(key, value) Makes a value available to @viewData("key") .WithSsr(SsrMode) / .WithoutSsr() Overrides the SSR mode for this response .WithSsrCache(duration, staleFor?) Reuses a server-rendered response for the same page JSON Pages without a handler MapInertia maps GET and HEAD to a rendered page, like Laravel's Route::inertia : The root template On the first visit the response is an HTML document. Inertia.Net reads app.html from the content root (configurable with RootView ), parses it once, and replaces these tokens: Token Output --- --- @inertia Without SSR: the page JSON script and the root element. With SSR: the server-rendered body. Required. @inertiaHead The SSR head tags joined with newlines. Empty without SSR. @vite("resources/js/app.tsx") Vite tags for one or more comma-separated entries. @viteReactRefresh The React Fast Refresh preamble while the dev server runs. Put it before @vite . @viewData("title") An HTML-encoded value passed with WithViewData . @@ A literal @ . Other @ characters, such as CSS at-rules and e-mail addresses, are left alone. Arguments accept single or double quotes. The page JSON is escaped with \uXXXX sequences, so a prop containing cannot break out of the script element. RootElementId (default app ) changes both the root element id and the data-page value. The client finds the page script by that id. app.html is read from disk at runtime. Add CopyToOutputDirectory and CopyToPublishDirectory so it is present after dotnet publish . Razor root view (MVC) With Inertia.Net.Mvc , the first-visit HTML can be a Razor view: "App" finds Views/Shared/App.cshtml . The view receives an InertiaRootViewContext model and uses tag helpers: takes comma-separated entries. SSR runs at most once per request and is shared by and . WithRootView("Other") takes Razor view names when the Razor root view is enabled. A custom root view Implement IInertiaRootView and register it before AddInertia : Page URL and path base The page object's url is the request PathBase, Path and QueryString. Behind a proxy that rewrites paths, set o.UrlResolver to return the URL the browser sees: Back() and the Vite asset URLs also respect the path base.

title: Installation
description: Install Inertia.Net, the optional MVC or FastEndpoints package, and the testing helpers.
body: Inertia.Net is split into small packages. Install the core package and one optional backend integration. Package Install when --- --- Inertia.Net always. The core adapter, Minimal API support, Vite, SSR, state store and antiforgery Inertia.Net.Mvc you use MVC controllers: ModelState filter, Razor root view and tag helpers Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints you use FastEndpoints: Send extensions, validation pre-processor and Precognition Inertia.Net.Testing in your test project: fluent assertions over Inertia responses Inertia.Net.Templates dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates : start a complete app Use the same version for every Inertia.Net package. The package version and the Inertia.js protocol version are separate numbers: Inertia.Net 1.5.3 implements Inertia.js v3. Requirements - .NET 10 SDK and an Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web project. - Node.js and npm for the frontend. Node is only needed at runtime when SSR is enabled. - An Inertia.js v3 client: @inertiajs/react , @inertiajs/vue3 or @inertiajs/svelte . Start from the template Choose --framework vue or --framework svelte for another client. The template includes working pages, a Todos form, validation, flash messages, CSRF protection and Vite configuration. Namespace and global usings The namespace is Inertia.Net and the static factory class is Inertia.Net.Inertia . C resolves a leading Inertia to the namespace, so Inertia.Render(...) does not compile outside the Inertia.Net namespace. The package's buildTransitive props file adds both global usings when enable is set, which is the default in new projects: Write Render(...) , Defer(...) , Once(...) , Back() and Location(...) unqualified. Set false and add using static Inertia.Net.Inertia; yourself, or call Inertia.Net.Inertia.Render(...) . HttpContext.Inertia() is an extension method and works as written. Next steps Add the four pieces every Inertia app needs: services, middleware, a root template and a client. Install React, Vue or Svelte and configure Vite for development and production.

title: TypeScript Types
description: Generate declarations for page props, shared props and flash data from your .NET contracts.
body: Inertia.Net can write TypeScript declarations for typed page props, shared props and flash data. They follow the app's JSON contracts (the HTTP JSON options and their source-generated contexts), so names, nullability and enum values match the page JSON. Configure generation The file is written when the app starts in Development, and only when its content changed. Commit it so tsc passes in CI without running the app. Shared props Shared props are inferred from the values passed to o.Share(...) ; dot keys nest. Factories and per-request shares are typed as unknown . o.TypeScript.SharedProps () replaces the inference with an explicit type. The InertiaConfig augmentation types usePage().props and flash . Prop members An InertiaProp member is optional (it can be deferred, optional or rescued) and unknown , unless [InertiaPropType(typeof(T))] names its value type. Mapping .NET TypeScript --- --- int , long , double , decimal , float number ( number \ bigint for 64-bit and larger with PreserveBigIntegers ) DateTime , DateTimeOffset , DateOnly , TimeOnly , Guid , byte[] string enum union of JSON values (string names with a string enum converter) dictionary Record polymorphic type union tagged with its discriminator nullable member T \ null Types missing from the JSON metadata (under Native AOT, register them in your context) are unknown , with a warning in the log. Number handling follows member settings, then type settings, then the global JSON options. Custom converter output is typed as unknown with a warning when its shape cannot be inferred. Props are written with the HTTP JsonOptions . MVC error keys use the MVC JsonOptions . If the two naming policies differ, generated prop names and validation error keys will not match.

title: Testing
description: Fluent assertions over Inertia responses and helpers for partial reloads and deferred props.
body: Inertia.Net.Testing has Laravel-style fluent assertions over Inertia responses and HttpClient helpers. It parses both JSON responses ( X-Inertia: true ) and the first-visit HTML , and decodes $bigint values. Failures throw InertiaAssertionException with a readable message, so it works with any test framework. Add public partial class Program; to your app when it uses top-level statements. Request helpers Helper Purpose --- --- InertiaGetAsync(url, version?, configure?) Sends an Inertia GET InertiaRequestAsync(method, url, content?, version?, configure?) Sends an Inertia request with any method GetInertiaPageAsync() Parses the response into an InertiaPage AssertInertiaAsync(assert) Parses, runs the assertions and returns the page Page assertions Component , Url , Version , HasFlash(key) , HasFlash(key, value) , MissingFlash(key) , HasDeferred(path) and HasDeferred(group, path) . Prop assertions On props and nested scopes (dot paths and array indexes allowed): Has(key) , Has(key, count) , Has(key, scope) , Has(key, count, firstItemScope) , HasAll , HasAny , Missing , MissingAll , Where(key, value) , Where(key, predicate) , WhereNot , WhereNull , WhereNotNull , WhereType(key, "string null") , WhereAllType , WhereContains(key, ...) , Count , CountBetween , Each(scope) , First(scope) and Dump() . Strict interaction tracking. Like Laravel, a nested scope fails when it contains properties you did not assert, unless you end it with Etc() . The root scope is not checked automatically: call .Interacted() at the end to enforce that every top-level prop was asserted. Partial reloads and deferred props InertiaPage replays the request with the right headers: ReloadOnlyAsync asserts that "users" is in the result; ReloadExceptAsync asserts that it is missing. InertiaPage members Props , Raw , Prop(path) , HasProp(path) , PropBigInteger(path) , DeferredProps , MergeProps , PrependProps , DeepMergeProps , MatchPropsOn , RescuedProps , SharedProps , ScrollProps , OnceProps , Flash , EncryptHistory , ClearHistory , PreserveFragment , PreserveBigIntegers . Flash and errors travel in a cookie across the redirect, so use a client that keeps cookies. Disable AllowAutoRedirect to assert the redirect itself, then follow it with a second InertiaGetAsync to read the flash or errors.

title: CSRF & Antiforgery
description: Protect forms with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
body: The Inertia client reads the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and sends its value as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on every request. UseInertiaAntiforgery() issues that cookie and validates it, so one call protects every form. What it does - Issue. Page loads (GET/HEAD requests that are Inertia requests or accept text/html ) get the request token in a script-readable, essential cookie ( HttpOnly off, SameSite=Lax , Path=/ , Secure per SecurePolicy ). Essential means a cookie-consent policy does not withhold it. - Validate. Every unsafe request (anything but GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE), with a JSON or a form body, Inertia or not, is checked with IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync . A plain cross-site HTML form post is rejected as well as a forged XHR. It also sets the antiforgery feature, so form-binding endpoints work without app.UseAntiforgery() . - Reject. A missing or wrong token gets 419 (page expired, as in Laravel); the handler does not run. - Opt out per endpoint with .DisableAntiforgery() (webhooks, test hooks), or for whole areas with ShouldValidate . Options OnRejected runs after UseInertia() ; returning Back() gives the tab a fresh token and a message instead of the client's error dialog. Lazy refresh By default every page load issues a fresh token, and antiforgery marks that response Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store (which also keeps the page out of the browser's back/forward cache). o.CookieRefresh = XsrfCookieRefresh.Lazy keeps a token that still validates. Such responses get no Set-Cookie and stay cacheable, and a token issued before a sign-in or sign-out is replaced on the next page load. Validating costs about what issuing does, so the gain is in the responses, not in CPU. Set your own Cache-Control on pages with private data. A session that expires or a sign-in that changes the user invalidates the token in an open tab; the next page load issues a new one. Returning Back() from OnRejected gives that tab a fresh token and a message. MVC and FastEndpoints UseInertiaAntiforgery() covers controllers too. [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] as a global filter still works, but is not needed. FastEndpoints is covered by the middleware; FastEndpoints' own EnableAntiforgery() is not needed for Inertia forms. Issue only UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN") (the 1.0 API) only writes the cookie. You then validate with app.UseAntiforgery() (form bodies only) and your own check for JSON bodies ( await antiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context) ). Prefer UseInertiaAntiforgery() . Troubleshooting 419 - Was the page loaded through the middleware? It sets the cookie. - Does the cookie reach the browser? Secure cookies are dropped on plain HTTP; behind a TLS-terminating proxy, configure forwarded headers or set CookieSecurePolicy.Always . - Do all instances share the Data Protection key ring? - Does UseAuthentication() run before the antiforgery middleware? - Did a sign-in or sign-out change the token? Reload the page, or use OnRejected . See Deploying for proxy and multi-instance settings.

title: Server-side Rendering
description: Render the first visit on Bun or Node, supervise the process from .NET, and fall back safely.
headings: 3. Let the app run Bun or Node
body: SSR renders the first visit on a JavaScript server using your client bundle, so crawlers and slow devices get HTML. Inertia XHR requests are never rendered on the server. 1. Build the SSR bundle Build both bundles: The client entry hydrates when the server rendered: Run the bundle with Bun or Node, or let the app start it: Build and run from a directory with node modules installed. The SSR build leaves node modules imports external. 2. Enable it A response can choose its own mode: The global mode decides first: Disabled is a kill switch no response can override. Otherwise the response's mode wins, then ExcludePaths , then the global mode. SSR runs only for first visits (the HTML response). The page JSON is posted to {url}/render , and { "head": [...], "body": "..." } is written into the root view. @inertiaHead outputs the head tags; @inertia outputs the body. 3. Let the app run Bun or Node A hosted service runs {Executable} {bundle} ( node by default; Bun works too) once per instance, logs stdout as Information and stderr as Warning under Inertia.Net.Ssr , and waits for every instance's GET /health . Occupied ports are refused before anything is spawned. Ssr.Urls is not used in managed mode. The executable is configurable. This documentation site builds a self-contained SSR bundle and runs it with Bun: o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n = n.Executable = "bun") . The default is node ; the bundle accepts either runtime. - An instance that exits is restarted after 1 second, doubling to 30 seconds. - An instance that stops answering its liveness check is killed and restarted the same way. - Shutdown stops the owned process trees without requesting /shutdown . - Nothing is spawned while the Vite dev server runs. - For external or remote servers, set Mode and Urls without UseNodeProcess() . The SSR server has no authentication. Anyone who can reach it can POST /render (CPU) or POST /shutdown , and its head and body are written into your pages verbatim. Listen on 127.0.0.1 . Before an instance takes renders, Inertia.Net tries the machine's non-loopback addresses on its port. If the instance answers there, it is stopped and an error is logged. AllowNetworkExposure = true keeps it running with a warning. A graceful shutdown stops the SSR process. If the .NET process is killed outright, the OS does not take the runtime with it. Use a process manager or container for hard-crash cleanup. 4. Development With the Vite hot file present (Development only), or o.Vite.DevServerUrl set, Inertia.Net posts to {viteDevUrl}/ inertia ssr . The endpoint is served by @inertiajs/vite , so you need no built bundle and no separate SSR server. BundlePath is ignored while the dev server runs. 5. Failures and fallbacks In Preferred mode every failure logs a warning and the page renders on the client. In Required mode it throws InertiaSsrException before the first byte is written, so the app's exception handler can still answer. Type Cause Opens the circuit --- --- --- connection Connection refused or reset. A refused connection is retried on another server. yes timeout Ssr.Timeout elapsed yes http Non-2xx answer without a structured error yes response Empty or malformed answer yes render The component threw (structured error from the renderer) no response-too-large Answer over MaxResponseBytes no overloaded No render slot within Concurrency.QueueTimeout , or the queue is full no circuit-open , not-ready , page-too-large , bundle-missing Skipped without a call no Circuit breaker. After CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold (default 5) consecutive failures that open the circuit, a server is skipped for BreakDuration (default 10 s). Then one render probes it: success closes the circuit, failure starts another break. A page that fails because of its own code never pauses the server. Render slots. Each server takes at most Concurrency.MaxActive renders at once (default 8, 0 for no limit) from this app instance, with up to MaxQueued (default 32) waiting at most QueueTimeout (default 250 ms). Renders that find no slot fall back immediately. 6. Several servers Each render goes to the server with the fewest renders in flight among those whose circuit is closed (ties rotate). Every server has its own slots, queue and circuit. Only a refused connection is retried on another server within the same deadline. Page props travel to the renderer, and its HTML goes into your pages unescaped, so it must be trusted. A plain http:// URL that is not loopback logs a warning at startup. Use HTTPS or a private network. 7. Health check The check reports what the renders have already shown, without calling the SSR servers: healthy while SSR is disabled, goes through the Vite dev server, or every server can take renders; degraded while some circuits are open or some managed instances are not ready; the registration's failure status (default unhealthy) when none can. Its data lists each server's state. 8. Observability Instrument Type Tags --- --- --- inertia.page.duration (s) histogram inertia.response , inertia.partial inertia.page.size (By) histogram inertia.response inertia.ssr.duration (s) histogram inertia.ssr.outcome inertia.ssr.queue.duration (s) histogram inertia.ssr.active up-down counter inertia.ssr.outcomes counter inertia.ssr.outcome , inertia.ssr.reason inertia.ssr.response.size (By) histogram inertia.ssr.circuit.state gauge inertia.ssr.endpoint inertia.ssr.circuit.transitions counter inertia.ssr.endpoint , to inertia.ssr.process.restarts counter cause inertia.props.rescued counter Tag values are bounded: no URLs, component names or user data. The inertia.render activity carries inertia.component ; the inertia.ssr activity carries inertia.ssr.endpoint , inertia.ssr.outcome and inertia.ssr.reason . Nothing is recorded unless a listener is attached. 9. Response cache A render depends only on the page JSON, so a page that many visitors see byte for byte the same can reuse its HTML: The key is the SHA-256 of the page JSON (component, props, url, version and the rest), so a new deploy or different props never reuse a stale render. Pages with per-user props make one entry per user; cache the pages that are shared. A hit is counted as inertia.ssr.outcomes{inertia.ssr.outcome=rendered, inertia.ssr.reason=cache} and bypasses the render slots and circuit breakers. Nothing is cached while the Vite dev server renders. Concurrent misses for the same page share one fill per app instance. Waiting counts against Ssr.Timeout ; cancelling a waiting request does not cancel the request filling the entry. With StaleFor , a render past its Duration is still served and rendered again after the response, like stale props. IInertiaCache.ClearSsrAsync() removes every render.

title: Validation & Error Bags
description: Redirect back with validation errors for Minimal APIs, MVC and FastEndpoints, and add Precognition.
body: Inertia forms post, expect a redirect, and read validation errors from props.errors on the next page. Inertia.Net performs the redirect and carries the errors across it. - A field maps to its first message. With o.WithAllErrors = true it maps to an array of all messages (the client's form.withAllErrors() expects that). - Error keys are the JSON names of the model members, one naming-policy conversion per segment: Address.Street becomes address.street . - Error bags. The client sends X-Inertia-Error-Bag: createUser when the form has errorBag="createUser" . Errors arrive as errors: { createUser: { email: "..." } } . Without the header, errors is the flat object { email: "..." } . A bag stored under a name other than default is always nested by bag name. Minimal API WithInertiaValidation() for a route or a route group. It requires services.AddValidation() for attribute validation. For an Inertia request that is not a GET, a failure becomes a redirect back (303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE) with the errors. Every other client still gets the normal 400 validation problem. A handler that returns TypedResults.ValidationProblem(...) , Results.ValidationProblem(...) or an HttpValidationProblemDetails is converted the same way. The built-in .NET 10 validation filter is added automatically and always runs outermost: it writes the 400 itself before any filter you add can see it. WithInertiaValidation() disables it on the endpoint and runs the same source-generated validation itself. Do not combine it with your own .DisableValidation() . To report errors yourself, without attribute validation: Back().WithErrors(IDictionary errors, string bag = "default") also takes arrays of messages. MVC AddInertiaMvc() registers a global filter. An Inertia non-GET request with an invalid ModelState is redirected back with the errors before the action runs, in the bag from X-Inertia-Error-Bag (default default ). [ApiController] controllers work too: their automatic 400 is replaced by the same redirect for Inertia requests. Binding failures get the generic message The value is invalid. , because their exception messages can expose internals. FastEndpoints c.UseInertia() adds a global pre-processor. A validation failure of an Inertia non-GET request becomes a redirect back with the errors; other requests keep FastEndpoints' 400 JSON. FluentValidation validators work as usual. c.UseInertia() sets c.Endpoints.Configurator . Pass your own configuration as its argument instead of setting the configurator separately. The pre-processor runs after an endpoint's own pre-processors, so one that already answered (a 403, say) wins. Precognition (live validation) Precognition validates a form as the user types, without running the handler. A request with Precognition: true is validated and answered with: - 204 and Precognition-Success: true when valid; - 422 and { "message": "...", "errors": { "field": ["..."] } } when not, limited to the fields in Precognition-Validate-Only ; - Precognition: true and Vary: Precognition on every response. WithInertiaPrecognition() is a superset of WithInertiaValidation() : normal Inertia validation redirects keep working. Any endpoint filter you add after it does not run for a precognitive request. In MVC, Precognition is not available. Client (Inertia v3 has it built in): Error bags in the client All errors for a field With the option on, errors.email is an array of every message instead of the first. State and redirects Validation errors travel in the state store across the redirect. By default that is an encrypted cookie; it can be a session or MVC TempData instead. See Flash data for the store choices and size limits.

title: Native AOT
description: Publish a Native AOT Inertia.Net app with source-generated JSON metadata.
body: Inertia.Net and Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints are annotated IsAotCompatible . A real app is published with Native AOT in CI ( tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke ) with zero trim and AOT warnings allowed. The library never reflects over your props: values are written with JsonTypeInfo from your JsonSerializerContext . 1. Register a JSON context Register every prop type and chain the context into the HTTP JSON options: Register the type that each loader returns and each plain value you place in InertiaProps , plus flash values that are not plain strings or numbers. The library's own context already covers string , bool , int , long , double , decimal , float , Guid , DateTime , DateTimeOffset , DateOnly , TimeOnly , TimeSpan , JsonElement , string[] , int[] , List , Dictionary , Dictionary , InertiaProps and Dictionary . Members of type InertiaProp are accepted by the source generator without any attribute. 2. Make validation models public The .NET 10 AddValidation() source generator skips internal types, and validation then silently does nothing. Only one AddValidation() call site per project is allowed. 3. Add ProblemDetails The non-Inertia 400 validation problem needs the ProblemDetails JSON metadata, or it cannot be serialized without reflection. 4. Avoid anonymous types Anonymous types do not work as props or flash values under AOT. Use InertiaProps , records or classes registered in the context. 5. Copy content files app.html and the Vite manifest are read from disk at runtime. Copy them to the publish directory, and set the content root to the binary's directory when it may run from elsewhere: 6. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints MVC is not AOT compatible (neither is MVC itself), so Inertia.Net.Mvc is not either. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints. 7. FastEndpoints source generation DiscoveredTypes is generated by the FastEndpoints.Generator package, in the namespace named after the assembly. See samples/FastEndpoints.Svelte . 8. Trim HTTP/3 The SSR client never uses HTTP/3, so it can be trimmed out: Cached props, the SSR cache, nonces, prefetching, MapInertia and the DevTools recorder are all AOT safe and covered by the smoke test. Set JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false in regular builds too. A missing JsonSerializable registration then fails in tests instead of only in the AOT publish. The reference app is tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke/Program.cs . Run it end to end with bash eng/aot-smoke.sh on Linux with clang and zlib installed.

title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
description: Common errors, their causes, and how to fix them.
headings: The Inertia page component was not found
A redirect to another site turns into a 409
The root view resolves outside the content root
The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409
The dev server tags do not appear
The root template was not found, or @inertia is missing
Validation errors do not show up (Minimal API)
Validation keys do not match my field names
InertiaProp values can only be serialized by Inertia.Net
Native AOT: JsonTypeInfo metadata was not provided
SSR does not run and there is no error
Several managed instances never become healthy
The SSR output is not hydrated
Does it work behind a path base?
Can I mix Razor Pages or views with Inertia pages?
body: Inertia.Render(...) does not compile 'Inertia' is a namespace . Call Render(...) unqualified. The namespace Inertia.Net shadows the class name outside the Inertia.Net namespace. The global usings come from the package's buildTransitive props and need enable . Without implicit usings, or with InertiaNetImplicitUsings set to false , add using static Inertia.Net.Inertia; . Inside a namespace that starts with Inertia.Net. , the name Inertia binds to the Inertia.Net.Inertia class. Source generators that emit non- global:: names starting with Inertia then break. Do not put your app's code under an Inertia.Net. namespace. Run npm run build , or start the dev server so the hot file exists in Development, or set o.Vite.ManifestPath / o.Vite.BuildDirectory . Check that Vite writes .vite/manifest.json ( build.manifest: true , Vite 5 and later) to wwwroot/build , and that the build output is part of what you deploy. The @vite("...") argument must equal the manifest key, which is the path relative to the Vite root. The error lists the available entries. Form submissions fail with 419 UseInertiaAntiforgery() rejected a request without a valid X-XSRF-TOKEN . Check that: - the page was loaded through the middleware (it sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie); - the cookie reaches the browser ( Secure on plain HTTP is dropped; see Deploying); - all instances share the Data Protection key ring; - UseAuthentication() runs before it. A sign-in or sign-out changes the token: reload the page, or return Back() from OnRejected . Exempt webhooks and token-authenticated APIs with .DisableAntiforgery() or ShouldValidate . The Inertia page component was not found o.Pages.Directory is set and the component passed to Render(...) has no page file there. Names match exactly, as the client's page resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems; the message suggests the closest page. Fix the name, or check Pages.Extensions when your pages use another extension. The check never runs outside Development. A redirect to another site turns into a 409 That is ConvertExternalRedirects (on by default): an Inertia request cannot follow a redirect to another origin, so it gets 409 + X-Inertia-Location and the client does a full visit. If it happens for your own host, the app is behind a proxy that does not forward the scheme (see Deploying), or use relative redirects. o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false disables the conversion. The root view resolves outside the content root RootView and WithRootView(...) take a path relative to the content root; absolute paths and .. are refused. Never derive them from request data. The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409 A 409 means the asset version differs between the client and the server. A loop means it never converges: usually the version changes on every request (a VersionResolver that returns a new value each time, or a manifest regenerated by a file watcher), or different instances behind a load balancer serve different builds. Use a stable version string. In Development the manifest hash changes after each vite build , which is expected once. The dev server tags do not appear The hot file is read only when ASPNETCORE ENVIRONMENT=Development . Check that wwwroot/hot exists and contains http://localhost:5173 , or set o.Vite.DevServerUrl . Remember base: '/' for the dev server in vite.config . The root template was not found, or @inertia is missing RootView is relative to the content root . Copy app.html to the output and publish directories ( CopyToOutputDirectory , CopyToPublishDirectory ). The template must contain @inertia . Flash data or errors disappear The state cookie is limited to about 4 KB by browsers. Flash less data, or use o.State.UseSession() . If the app runs on several instances, share Data Protection keys. If the cookie is never sent back, check the cookie Secure flag on HTTP behind a proxy that does not forward X-Forwarded-Proto . Validation errors do not show up (Minimal API) Use .WithInertiaValidation() on the endpoint. Without it, the built-in AddValidation() filter returns a 400 problem details that the Inertia client cannot use. Make sure the model types are public . Validation keys do not match my field names Keys go through the JSON naming policy per segment ( Address.Street becomes address.street ). In MVC the policy is the one in the MVC JsonOptions . The page itself is written with the HTTP JsonOptions : keep both policies aligned. InertiaProp values can only be serialized by Inertia.Net An InertiaProp ended up somewhere Inertia.Net does not walk: a Flash(...) value, a read-only dictionary type that does not implement IDictionary , or a type with a custom converter. Lists, typed dictionaries ( Dictionary with any key type), object members and IDictionary are walked. Put props in InertiaProps , or declare the member as InertiaProp (or object ) on the typed page object. Native AOT: JsonTypeInfo metadata was not provided Add the type to your JsonSerializerContext and chain it with ConfigureHttpJsonOptions . Setting JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false in regular builds finds these early. See Native AOT. SSR does not run and there is no error SSR falls back to client rendering on any failure. Look for the warnings Inertia SSR failed (...) and Inertia SSR skipped (...) . The first includes the server's hint. Check o.Ssr.Mode , Urls , that the Node server is running ( GET /health ; with UseNodeProcess() look for Inertia.Net.Ssr log lines), that BundlePath points at the built file, that the path is not in ExcludePaths , and that the page is under MaxPageBytes . Set Mode = SsrMode.Required in Development to surface the failure. SSR skipped (circuit-open) or (overloaded) - circuit-open : the server failed CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold times in a row and is skipped for BreakDuration ; the earlier Inertia SSR failed warnings say why. - overloaded : more renders arrived than Concurrency.MaxActive plus MaxQueued , or one waited longer than QueueTimeout . Add servers or instances, or raise the limits if the server has headroom. Several managed instances never become healthy Every instance must listen on its own port: the SSR entry has to read process.env.INERTIA SSR PORT . A bundle built only by @inertiajs/vite listens on its baked-in port. The SSR output is not hydrated Use the hydrating client entry shown in Server-side rendering and build both bundles from the same sources. The SSR body is marked data-server-rendered="true" . Does it work behind a path base? Yes. The page url keeps the path base, the Vite URLs include it, and Back() works. Can I use Newtonsoft.Json? No. Props use System.Text.Json with the HTTP JSON options. Can I mix Razor Pages or views with Inertia pages? Yes. Inertia handles only the endpoints that return Render(...) . The middleware leaves other responses alone, apart from Vary: X-Inertia .

title: Infinite Scroll
description: Merge pages of items and report paging metadata to the InfiniteScroll client component.
body: Scroll(...) merges the items inside a value (the wrapper , "data" by default) and reports paging metadata to the client component. The client Metadata ScrollMetadata(PageName, PreviousPage, NextPage, CurrentPage) is a record. Page values can be int , long , string or null (cursor paging uses strings). Metadata comes from the metadata: argument, or from the value if it implements IProvidesScrollMetadata . Without either, the render throws with a message naming the prop. The client sends X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent: prepend when scrolling up. The wrapper is then reported under prependProps instead of mergeProps . scrollProps[path].reset is true when the request lists the path in X-Inertia-Reset . Combining with other props Scroll(...) accepts the five loader shapes, and .Defer() , .Once() and .Rescue() combine with it: A deferred scroll prop reports "posts.data" just like a resolved one. This is a deliberate fix of an inertia-laravel quirk. Infinite scroll is also a payload-size tool. Load 10 to 20 items per page instead of sending an unbounded list on the first request.

title: Partial Reloads
description: Reload only the props a page needs with only and except filters.
body: The Inertia client can reload the current page and ask for a subset of its props. This is how deferred props, polling and infinite scroll work, and you can use it directly for dashboard refresh buttons and filters. From the client router.visit('/users', { only: ['users'] }) works for a new page too. The client sends: Header Meaning --- --- X-Inertia-Partial-Component The component being rendered X-Inertia-Partial-Data The only list X-Inertia-Partial-Except The except list Filtering applies only when the partial component equals the component being rendered. Server behavior - Paths are dot paths and match on a . boundary. only: ["user"] includes user.name ; only: ["user.name"] includes user.name and keeps user as a container. - except beats only . Always(...) ignores both. - The children of a value produced by a loader are not filtered. Nested literal InertiaProps are. - Loaders of excluded props never run. - Selecting an array descendant ( rows.1.extra ) reloads the complete array, including sibling fields and nested loaders. A descendant except excludes the entire array; Always still wins. - Omitted or rescued direct array elements retain their positions as null . - A missing or empty list header means “no filter”, which differs from an empty list. Always(...) is sent even when a partial reload does not ask for it. Use it for props the page cannot render without; do not use it for expensive data. What the client keeps A reloaded prop replaces the client's value by default. A prop resolved from a loader is sent in full. To combine values instead, use merge props. Deferred and once props Deferred props are loaded through partial reloads. X-Inertia-Partial-Data asks for the deferred group, and the server records which deferred props it has sent. Once props that the reload asks for always resolve. The client sends X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props with the keys it already holds, so the server can skip them while keeping the onceProps metadata. Testing partial reloads Inertia.Net.Testing replays the request with the right headers: ReloadOnlyAsync asserts that the requested prop is present; ReloadExceptAsync asserts that it is missing.

title: Introduction
description: Inertia.Net is a .NET 10 server adapter for Inertia.js v3. Build React, Vue and Svelte apps without a separate API.
body: Inertia.Net connects ASP.NET Core to the Inertia.js v3 client. Your endpoints return pages and props; the client renders them as React, Vue or Svelte components. The first visit is a normal HTML response, and later visits are Inertia requests that update the page without a full reload. It is an adapter, not a framework. Routing, authentication, authorization, validation and persistence stay in ASP.NET Core. There is no separate JSON API to design and no client-side router to keep in sync. How it works The first request returns HTML with the page object embedded. Inertia links and form submissions request the next page in the background and swap the component while the browser keeps its state. Your .NET app still owns the request. The adapter adds the protocol middleware, prop resolution, redirect semantics, flash data and asset tags. What you get Minimal APIs, MVC controllers and FastEndpoints share the same core package and protocol behavior. Lazy, optional, deferred, merged, once, cached, rescued and infinite-scroll props. CSRF cookies, encrypted state, asset versioning, proxy support and SSR supervision. Props are written through System.Text.Json metadata. No reflection over your page objects. Feature matrix Minimal API MVC controllers FastEndpoints --- :---: :---: :---: Package Inertia.Net Inertia.Net + Inertia.Net.Mvc Inertia.Net + Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints Render / Back / Location Render(...) returns IResult same, return IResult from an action Send.InertiaAsync(...) or return the result Validation redirect with errors .WithInertiaValidation() ModelState filter (global) c.UseInertia() pre-processor Precognition .WithInertiaPrecognition() not available c.UseInertia() Razor root view no ( app.html template) optional (tag helpers) no ( app.html template) Native AOT yes no (MVC itself is not AOT) yes (with the FastEndpoints source generator) The client packages are @inertiajs/react , @inertiajs/vue3 and @inertiajs/svelte , all version 3. Inertia.Net does not support v2 clients. This documentation site This site is an Inertia.Net app. The sidebar, search, docs pages and theme switcher are React components rendered by an ASP.NET Core Minimal API. Navigation uses Inertia links, and the source is in docs/Inertia.Net.Docs so it doubles as a real example. Requirements - .NET 10 SDK - Node.js and npm to build the frontend (at runtime only when SSR is enabled) - An Inertia.js v3 client package for React, Vue or Svelte Use the starter template: dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates , then dotnet new inertia -n MyApp --framework react . It includes working pages, a form with validation, flash messages, CSRF and Vite configuration. Next steps - Install the packages in an existing app. - Follow the quick start for a minimal end-to-end setup. - Read the props reference when you are ready to model page data.

title: Deploying Behind a Proxy
description: Forwarded headers, secure cookies, compression, asset caching and multi-instance state.
body: Behind a load balancer or reverse proxy that terminates TLS, Kestrel sees plain HTTP unless the scheme is forwarded. Without it, the state and XSRF-TOKEN cookies are not marked Secure , and the version-mismatch 409 sends an http:// X-Inertia-Location . Forwarded headers When the scheme cannot be forwarded, force the cookies: Multi-instance state On several instances, share the Data Protection key ring so the state cookie and antiforgery tokens can be read by every instance: Using the session store? Sessions must be shared too (for example Redis). The default cookie store only needs shared Data Protection keys. Keep the SSR server on loopback on each instance. See Server-side rendering. Compression Page JSON and HTML compress five to ten times. Compress at the proxy, or in the app: Over HTTPS the middleware compresses only with o.EnableForHttps = true . Review BREACH for your pages first: Inertia.Net keeps the antiforgery token in a cookie, not in the body, but a page that reflects request input next to a secret is still exposed. Asset caching Vite puts a content hash in every built file name, so files under build/assets can be cached for good: app.MapStaticAssets() does the same with build-time Brotli when the client is built before dotnet publish , so the files are in wwwroot when the static web assets manifest is generated. Path base Use app.UsePathBase("/app") before UseInertia() . The page url , Vite URLs and Back() include the path base. If a proxy rewrites paths, set o.UrlResolver to return the browser-visible URL. Health and readiness The SSR health check is covered in Server-side rendering. Deployment checklist - [ ] npm run build runs before dotnet publish , or wwwroot/build is copied into the publish output. - [ ] app.html is copied to the publish output. - [ ] Forwarded headers are configured, or cookies are forced secure. - [ ] Data Protection keys are shared between instances. - [ ] Static assets under /build/assets are cached as immutable. - [ ] Response compression is enabled at the proxy or in the app. - [ ] SSR listens on loopback and its bundle is deployed when SSR is enabled. - [ ] The client build and server build are the same version, so X-Inertia-Version converges.

title: Flash Data
description: Carry a one-time message, toast or typed value across a redirect.
body: Flash data is carried across the redirect (and any further redirects) and consumed by the next response that is not a redirect. It appears as page.flash , only when there is some. Read it with usePage().flash or the onFlash visit callback: The TypeScript generator can write a Flash type for you. Call o.TypeScript.FlashData () ; see TypeScript types. Where state is kept Flash data, errors, clearHistory and preserveFragment set during a request that ends in a redirect (or a Location() / fragment 409 ) are saved in an IInertiaStateStore and loaded at the start of the next request. If that request redirects again, the state is carried on, so Back() to a URL that itself redirects still shows the flash. Otherwise its response consumes it. The state is also kept when the response is the version-mismatch 409 . Encrypted cookie (default) The default store is an encrypted cookie named .Inertia.State . It is protected with ASP.NET Core Data Protection, HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , and works without sessions and under Native AOT. Tampered or undecryptable cookies are ignored and deleted. It logs a warning above about 4 KB because browsers drop larger cookies. Session store Use the session store when flash data can be large or must not reach the browser, and you already run sessions. MVC TempData store This keeps the state in MVC TempData, so it follows your TempData provider: the default cookie provider, or AddSessionStateTempDataProvider() with AddSession() and app.UseSession() before app.UseInertia() . It works for Minimal API endpoints too, because the store saves TempData itself. Not Native AOT compatible. Your own store Implement IInertiaStateStore and register it before AddInertia : The methods move opaque bytes; the format is Inertia.Net's. Choosing a store Store Use when --- --- Encrypted cookie Default. Stateless, AOT safe, about 4 KB limit. Session Flash data can be large or must not reach the browser, and sessions already exist. TempData The app standardizes on MVC TempData, or you want to switch providers without changing code. Custom You need a shared store across instances or a different transport. In a multi-instance deployment, configure Data Protection with a shared key ring. Otherwise the cookie written by one instance cannot be read by another. History flags encryptHistory is written only when set and is not carried across redirects. clearHistory and preserveFragment go through the state store and apply to the next page rendered after the redirects, then are consumed. See Redirects and history.

title: Shared Data
description: Share props with every page, statically or per request, and control the shared prop key list.
body: Shared props are merged into every page. A page prop with the same key wins. Register shared values Share values from anywhere with an HttpContext , such as middleware or a handler: The value can be any prop, including another factory: plans is resolved once and kept by the client across visits. The shared prop key list The top-level shared keys are listed in the page object so the client can keep them across navigations: errors is always shared, so the list always contains at least "errors" . Turn the list off with: When to use shared props Use shared props for values that every page needs and that are cheap to compute: - the signed-in user or tenant name - the application name and locale - feature flags - a once-per-client value such as a plan catalogue Keep large or page-specific data in page props. Shared props are considered on every page response, including partial reloads, so keep them cheap or wrap an expensive value in Once . Wrapping a shared value in Once is the equivalent of Laravel's shareOnce . The client keeps the value across visits and sends X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props ; the loader does not run again until the value expires. TypeScript The generated declarations infer shared props from the values passed to o.Share(...) . Factories and per-request shares are typed as unknown ; use o.TypeScript.SharedProps () when you want an explicit shape. See TypeScript types.

title: Migrating from Other Adapters
description: Map an InertiaCore-style API to Inertia.Net and check the behavior differences.
body: The API is close to the Laravel adapter's names. The table maps the typical InertiaCore-style API (kapi2289/InertiaCore and its forks). Check names against the version you use. Other adapters Inertia.Net --- --- Inertia.Render("Users/Index", new { users }) Render("Users/Index", new InertiaProps { ["users"] = users }) , or a typed props object return Inertia.Render(...) in a controller ( Task ) return Render(...) as IResult (MVC executes it) Inertia.Lazy(() = ...) / LazyProp Optional(() = ...) (never on first load) or Prop(() = ...) (lazy, included by default) Inertia.Defer(...) / Inertia.Defer(..., "group") Defer(..., group: "group") Inertia.Always(...) Always(...) Inertia.Merge(...) / DeepMerge Merge(...) , DeepMerge(...) , plus .Prepend() , .MatchOn() (not supported) Once(...) , Scroll(...) , .Rescue() , .Parallel() , .Cache(key, duration) Inertia.Share("key", value) o.Share("key", value) , o.Share("key", ctx = ...) , or ctx.Inertia().Share(...) Inertia.Location(url) Location(url) Inertia.Back() Back() / Back(fallback) Inertia.ClearHistory() , Inertia.EncryptHistory() ctx.Inertia().ClearHistory() , ctx.Inertia().EncryptHistory() (per request, no shared state) Inertia.Html(...) / Inertia.Head in Layout.cshtml app.html with @inertia , @inertiaHead , @vite(...) , or the Razor tag helpers Flash via TempData or session ctx.Inertia().Flash(...) , Back().WithFlash(...) (encrypted cookie by default) ModelState errors in session MVC: AddInertiaMvc() ; Minimal API: .WithInertiaValidation() ; FastEndpoints: c.UseInertia() Version option or manifest hashing per request o.Version , o.VersionResolver , or the cached manifest hash SSR options ( UseSsr , SsrUrl ) o.Ssr.Mode , o.Ssr.Urls , o.Ssr.ExcludePaths , Render(...).WithSsr(...) Behavior differences to check - v3 only. There is no v2 client support. Upgrade the client packages to v3. The first page is the element, not a data-page attribute on the root div. - Props are resolved without reflection. Anonymous types need reflection-enabled serialization, and AOT apps register a JsonSerializerContext . - HTTP JSON options. Props serialize with the HTTP JSON options (camelCase by default), not Newtonsoft. - Version check before the handler. A stale client gets a 409 before your endpoint runs. - State is an encrypted cookie by default. Flash, errors and history flags use it unless you opt into the session store. Upgrading Inertia.Net Package upgrade notes live in the repository: - 1.4 upgrade notes - 1.3 upgrade notes - 1.1 upgrade notes Update all Inertia.Net packages together. Mixing 1.5 with 1.4 packages can compile but produce different protocol output.

title: Performance
description: Memory and hosting guidance, payload limits and the design choices behind the adapter.
body: Benchmarks cover page rendering, partial reloads, deferred props, SSR, caching and state storage. These controlled microbenchmarks are not production throughput estimates. Memory and hosting The useful planning number is not a microbenchmark; it is how much memory the whole process needs at rest and under load. These are reference points measured on Linux x64 after the first request, not guarantees: App shape RSS at rest Plan for --- ---: ---: Inertia.Net JIT app, no database ( samples/MinimalApi.React ) about 90 MB 256–512 MB Inertia.Net Native AOT app ( tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke ) about 42 MB 128–256 MB Small JIT todo: Minimal API + EF Core + SQLite + cookie auth roughly 120–180 MB 256–512 MB Small Native AOT todo: source-generated JSON + SQLite roughly 45–70 MB 128–256 MB Add managed Bun SSR +30–60 MB for the Bun process add 128 MB headroom The two Inertia.Net baseline rows were measured from this repository on Linux x64; the todo rows are planning ranges, not benchmark claims. The JIT todo range includes the runtime, EF Core, SQLite, authentication and a small working set. PostgreSQL or MongoDB, image processing and a large cache move it upward; measure your own app under realistic concurrency. Native AOT removes most JIT and reflection overhead, but it does not make EF Core or a database free. For containers: - Set a memory limit rather than relying on the host. - Leave headroom for the GC, the OS page cache and request bursts. - Expect SSR to add a second process. If the Bun renderer is optional, SsrMode.Preferred lets the app fall back to client rendering when it is unavailable. - Profile with real page sizes. A dashboard with deferred props and a paginated feed behaves very differently from a page that serializes every row. The benchmark project still has the throughput and allocation probes: Targeted probes: --render-probe , --ssr-probe , --mvc-probe , --payload-probe and --cache-probe . Payload size The page JSON is fully buffered before the first byte is sent, so a failing loader never produces a half-written 200 . Each concurrent request therefore holds its whole page in memory (pooled, and sized from the component's recent pages). Keep pages well under a megabyte: - paginate with Scroll - defer slow data with Defer - load on demand with Optional - use a partial reload for refresh buttons and filters Ssr.MaxPageBytes keeps larger pages off the SSR server and Ssr.MaxResponseBytes bounds its answer; neither limits the props. Design notes - Single pass. One recursive walk filters props, runs loaders, writes JSON to a Utf8JsonWriter and collects the metadata. There is no intermediate object tree. - Pooled buffers. The page is written to a pooled IBufferWriter , and the path tracker is a pooled char[] . A path becomes a string only when metadata needs it. - Version check before the handler. A stale client costs one header comparison and a 409 . - No per-request mutable singletons. Per-request state lives in an InertiaFeature on HttpContext.Features , so concurrent requests cannot leak history or flash settings into one another. - Plain DTOs take the fast path. A POCO, list or typed dictionary is walked only when its type can hold InertiaProp values ( InertiaProp , object or dictionary members/elements; cached per type). Everything else is one Serialize call. - UTF-8 throughout. SSR output and the MVC tag helpers write UTF-8 bytes; nothing large is materialized as a .NET string. - Cached assets. The Vite manifest is parsed once, the root template is parsed once into pre-encoded UTF-8 segments, and the production tags are pre-rendered per entry set and path base. The version is a precomputed string compared ordinally. A missing manifest, template or SSR bundle is re-checked at most once per second. - Sync loaders stay sync. Func loaders are not wrapped in closures. Most per-request allocation in a real handler is the props you build, not the render.

title: Asset Versioning
description: Tell the client when its JavaScript and CSS are stale, and reload once when they are.
body: The asset version tells the client when its assets are stale. The server resolves it in this order: 1. InertiaOptions.VersionResolver(HttpContext) , when it returns non-null; 2. else InertiaOptions.Version ; 3. else a hash of the Vite manifest (the first 16 bytes of its SHA-256, in hex), computed once and recomputed in Development when the file changes; 4. else "" . How the client checks it When an Inertia GET carries a different X-Inertia-Version , the server answers 409 with X-Inertia-Location (the absolute request URL) and X-Inertia-Version , and the client performs a full page reload. The check runs before your handler , so no work is wasted rendering a page that will be thrown away. Other methods never get this 409 . Choosing a version - Vite manifest hash (default). Nothing to configure. A new build changes the manifest and the version. - Assembly version or build id. Good when the client build is not tied to the manifest, or when several apps share assets. - Per-request version. Useful for multi-tenant apps with different frontend builds per tenant. A VersionResolver that returns a random value on every call makes the client reload forever. Different instances behind a load balancer must serve the same build, or the client will bounce between versions. Path base The version check and X-Inertia-Location use the request URL. Behind a path base or reverse proxy, configure forwarded headers so the scheme and host match the browser's URL. See Deploying.
